stem: The graphs of the linear functions \(f\) and \(g\) are shown in the \(xy\)-plane. For which values of \(x\) is \(f(x) > g(x)\)?
solution: The graphs intersect at \((2, 3)\), so \(f(x) = g(x)\) when \(x = 2\).
To the right of \(x = 2\), the graph of \(f\), which rises, lies above the graph of \(g\), which falls.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses the \(y\)-coordinate of the intersection point, 3, instead of its \(x\)-coordinate, 2.
explanation.B: Correct. The graphs cross at \(x = 2\), and the graph of \(f\) is above the graph of \(g\) to the right of that point.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses the \(y\)-coordinate of the intersection point and the wrong side of it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. For \(x < 2\), the graph of \(f\) lies below the graph of \(g\), so \(f(x) < g(x)\).

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'B': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
x = symbols('x')
f, g = [sympify(c['expr']) for c in figure['curves']]
sol = solve_univariate_inequality(f > g, x, relational=False)
assert sol == Interval.open(2, oo)
P = lambda s: value(s.replace('\\le', '<=').replace('\\ge', '>='))
S = lambda s: solve_univariate_inequality(P(s), x, relational=False)
assert S(choices[answer]) == sol
assert all(S(choices[k]) != sol for k in choices if k != answer)
